title: Nodes & Pods — CPU and eBPF kernel metrics
description: Node CPU utilization/load and non-pod CPU attribution (services, kernel threads, kernel functions) plus per-pod run-queue latency, CFS throttle stalls, TCP retransmits/RSTs, block IO latency and OOM kills from ebpf_exporter, joined by pod UID.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: Use thanos-querier (or anything that sees both kube_pod_info and the exporter metrics).

panels.title: Pods observed
panels.description: Pods (matching the filters) whose threads were scheduled in the last 5m.

targets.expr: count((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_count[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))

panels.title: Nodes reporting
panels.description: ebpf-exporter targets currently up.

targets.expr: count(up{job="ebpf-exporter"} == 1)

panels.title: Programs detached
panels.description: eBPF programs that failed to attach anywhere. Should be 0 — see the Exporter health row.

targets.expr: count(ebpf_exporter_ebpf_program_attached == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Worst pod: CPU waits > 10 ms
panels.description: Highest share of run-queue waits longer than 10 ms across the selected pods (last 5m).

targets.expr: max((1 - sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.01"}[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_count[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) >= 0)

panels.title: TCP retransmits / s
panels.description: Total TCP retransmissions across the selected pods.

targets.expr: sum((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_tcp_retransmits_total[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: OOM kills (range)
panels.description: Kernel OOM kills inside the selected pods over the dashboard time range.

targets.expr: sum(increase(ebpf_exporter_pod_oom_kills_total[$__range]) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Nodes — CPU utilization, load and contention
panels.description: One row per node, last 5m. Load/core > 1 means more runnable threads than CPUs. 'Pods' threads waiting' and 'run-queue p99' come from eBPF and show what that load costs the pods: high load with low waits is harmless (often D-state/IO), low util with high waits points at pinning, CFS bandwidth or a few hot cores.

targets.expr: 1 - avg by (node) (label_replace(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}[5m]), "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

max by (node) (label_replace(node_load1{instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")) / count by (node) (label_replace(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

max by (node) (label_replace(node_load15{instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")) / count by (node) (label_replace(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

sum by (node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu", node=~"$node"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / sum by (node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu", node=~"$node"})
sum by (node) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (node) max by (uid, node) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node"}))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (node, le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[5m])))
count by (node) (label_replace(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Node CPU utilization — top $topk nodes
panels.description: 1 − idle across all cores, from node-exporter.

targets.expr: topk($topk, 1 - avg by (node) (label_replace(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]), "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")))

panels.title: Node load1 per core — top $topk nodes
panels.description: node_load1 / CPU count. Linux load includes uninterruptible (IO) sleep, so cross-check with the run-queue panels before blaming CPU.

targets.expr: topk($topk, max by (node) (label_replace(node_load1{instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")) / count by (node) (label_replace(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}, "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")))

panels.title: CPU time by mode (selected nodes)
panels.description: Where the busy time goes. High system/softirq points at networking or kernel work; steal at an oversubscribed hypervisor (KubeVirt workers); iowait isn't really CPU busy.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle", instance=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", instance=~"$node"}))

panels.title: Pods' threads waiting for CPU — top $topk nodes
panels.description: eBPF run-queue wait summed over every pod on the node = average number of pod threads that are runnable but not running. Rising here while CPU util is flat = contention, not lack of capacity.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (node) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (node) max by (uid, node) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Pods on selected nodes — top CPU users and top CPU waiters
panels.description: Union of the 50 pods using the most CPU and the 50 waiting the most (bounded even with thousands of pods in scope). High 'CPU used' above request = who drives the node; high 'Threads waiting' / 'Waits > 1 ms' with modest usage = who suffers. Throttled pods are capped by their own limit, not by the node.

targets.expr: (sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

(sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu"}) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

(sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="cpu"}) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

(sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

((1 - sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.001"}[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_count[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) >= 0) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

(sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_cfs_throttled_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) and on (namespace, pod) (topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node=~"$node", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) or topk(50, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))))

panels.title: Node CPU — who is using it (eBPF sampling)
Node CPU by owner (cores, selected nodes)
panels.description: Sampled at 49 Hz on every CPU. Pods vs. everything that isn't a pod: node services (kubelet, crio, ovs, NetworkManager, journald…) and kernel threads (kswapd, kworker, ksoftirqd, irq/…). Interrupt/softirq work that hits a busy CPU is charged to whatever was running there.

targets.expr: sum by (owner) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(rate(ebpf_exporter_node_cpu_samples_total{node=~"$node", context!="idle"}[$__rate_interval]), "owner", "pods", "context", "pod"), "owner", "node services (non-pod processes)", "context", "system"), "owner", "kernel threads", "context", "kernel")) / 49

sum(rate(ebpf_exporter_node_kernel_function_samples_total{node=~"$node", context="idle", function!~"(intel_idle.*|poll_idle|default_idle.*|acpi_idle.*|acpi_safe_halt|cpuidle_enter.*|mwait_idle.*|.*safe_halt|cpu_idle_poll.*|do_idle|arch_cpu_idle.*|cpu_startup_entry|amd_e400_idle|haltpoll.*)"}[$__rate_interval])) / 49

panels.title: Top non-pod CPU consumers — top $topk (cores)
panels.description: system = non-pod cgroup (systemd service/scope); kernel = kernel thread, per-CPU/instance suffixes folded (kworker/3:1 → kworker, kswapd0 → kswapd).

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (context, name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_cpu_samples_total{node=~"$node", context=~"system|kernel"}[$__rate_interval])) / 49)

panels.title: Non-pod CPU by service / kernel thread (cores, last 5m)
panels.description: High 'kernel mode' on a service usually means syscall/IO/allocation overhead it triggers — see the kernel function panels to the right.

targets.expr: sum by (context, name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_cpu_samples_total{node=~"$node", context=~"system|kernel"}[5m])) / 49
sum by (context, name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_cpu_samples_total{node=~"$node", context=~"system|kernel", mode="user"}[5m])) / 49
sum by (context, name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_cpu_samples_total{node=~"$node", context=~"system|kernel", mode="kernel"}[5m])) / 49

panels.title: Kernel CPU by subsystem (cores) — context: $kctx
panels.description: Kernel-mode samples grouped by function-name heuristics. 'slab (SLUB)' = kmem_cache/kmalloc/kfree and the slab paths; 'memcg charging' = cgroup memory accounting (often riding on slab allocations). Use the 'Kernel context' filter to see whether it happens on behalf of pods, node services or kernel threads.

targets.expr: sum by (subsystem) (ebpf:node_kernel_subsystem_cores:rate2m{node=~"$node", context=~"$kctx"})

panels.title: Top kernel functions — top $topk (cores) — context: $kctx
panels.description: Kernel functions where CPU was sampled (idle-loop functions excluded). A function under 'idle' context ran from an interrupt on an otherwise idle CPU.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (function, context) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_kernel_function_samples_total{node=~"$node", context=~"$kctx", function!~"(intel_idle.*|poll_idle|default_idle.*|acpi_idle.*|acpi_safe_halt|cpuidle_enter.*|mwait_idle.*|.*safe_halt|cpu_idle_poll.*|do_idle|arch_cpu_idle.*|cpu_startup_entry|amd_e400_idle|haltpoll.*)"}[$__rate_interval])) / 49)

panels.title: CPU waits > 1 ms (share) — top $topk pods
panels.description: Share of a pod's run-queue waits (runnable → on-CPU) longer than 1 ms. High with low CPU usage = noisy neighbours or CPU-pinning contention, not your limit. Per-pod data uses 1 ms / 10 ms thresholds to keep series low at thousands of pods; the full distribution is per node below.

targets.expr: topk($topk, (1 - sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.001"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) >= 0)

panels.title: Run-queue wait (avg runnable threads waiting) — top $topk pods
panels.description: Seconds spent waiting for a CPU per second = average number of this pod's threads sitting on a run queue. 1.0 means one thread is always waiting.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Run-queue latency distribution (selected nodes, all tasks)
panels.description: Full distribution of run-queue waits for every task on the selected nodes (pods, services, kernel threads). exp2 buckets, 1 µs … 4.2 s.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Run-queue latency p99 per node (all tasks) — top $topk nodes
panels.description: Node-level p99 from the full exp2 histogram. Compare nodes: a high p99 here with moderate CPU util means contention on a few cores (pinning, IRQ affinity, CFS bandwidth), not node capacity.

targets.expr: topk($topk, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (node, le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: CFS throttled time — top $topk pods
panels.description: Seconds per second that the pod's per-CPU run queues were frozen by CFS bandwidth control (cpu.max). Summed across CPUs, so it can exceed 1.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_cfs_throttled_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Throttle stalls > 10 ms (share) — top $topk pods
panels.description: Share of a pod's CFS throttle stalls longer than 10 ms (the per-pod buckets are 10 ms and 80 ms of the 100 ms period). cAdvisor only tells you *that* you were throttled; long stalls mean the quota runs out early in every period — latency spikes for request-serving pods.

targets.expr: topk($topk, (1 - sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_cfs_throttled_seconds_bucket{le="0.01"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_cfs_throttled_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) >= 0)

panels.title: TCP retransmits / s — top $topk pods
panels.description: Retransmitted segments, attributed via the socket's cgroup (works for timer/softirq-driven retransmits).

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_tcp_retransmits_total[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: TCP RSTs sent / s — top $topk pods
panels.description: Resets sent by full sockets owned by the pod (aborts, closes with unread data). RSTs to closed ports have no owning socket and aren't counted.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_tcp_resets_sent_total[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: TCP RSTs received / s — top $topk pods
panels.description: Connection refused / peer aborts seen by the pod. Spikes usually mean a dependency restarting or a load balancer killing idle connections.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) ((sum by (uid) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_tcp_resets_received_total[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Block IOs > 10 ms (share) — top $topk pod/op
panels.description: Share of a pod's block requests that took longer than 10 ms from allocation to completion (like iostat await, incl. IO-scheduler queueing), attributed by the bio's blkcg (buffered writeback is charged to the pod that dirtied the pages). Network/FUSE filesystems (NFS, CephFS) don't pass the block layer.

targets.expr: topk($topk, (1 - sum by (namespace, pod, operation) ((sum by (uid, operation) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_block_io_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.01"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod, operation) ((sum by (uid, operation) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_block_io_latency_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"}))) >= 0)

panels.title: Block IOPS — top $topk pod/op
panels.description: Completed block requests per second.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod, operation) ((sum by (uid, operation) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_block_io_latency_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Block IO avg latency — top $topk pod/op
panels.description: Mean latency (sum / count). Compare with the >10 ms share to spot tail-latency pods.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod, operation) ((sum by (uid, operation) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_block_io_latency_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) / sum by (namespace, pod, operation) ((sum by (uid, operation) (rate(ebpf_exporter_pod_block_io_latency_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Block IO latency p99 per node — top $topk nodes
panels.description: Full exp2 distribution over all block IO on the node (pods, services, kernel). A node-wide p99 jump that isn't in any single pod usually means the device or the storage backend, not a noisy pod.

targets.expr: topk($topk, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (node, le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_block_io_read_latency_seconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))))
topk($topk, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (node, le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_block_io_write_latency_seconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: OOM kills in range
panels.description: Kernel OOM kills by victim process. Keyed by pod (not container), so kills survive the container restart that follows.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, pod, comm) (increase(ebpf_exporter_pod_oom_kills_total[$__range]) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})) > 0

panels.title: OOM kills — top $topk pods
panels.description: OOM kills per interval. Includes kills of sidecars and child processes that don't restart the container.

targets.expr: topk($topk, sum by (namespace, pod) (increase(ebpf_exporter_pod_oom_kills_total[$__rate_interval]) * on (uid) group_left (namespace, pod) max by (uid, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", node=~"$node"})))

panels.title: Attached programs per node
panels.description: Expected: 8 per node (runqlat 1, cfs 1, tcp 3, block 1, oom 1, cpu profile 1).

targets.expr: sum by (node) (ebpf_exporter_ebpf_program_attached)

panels.title: eBPF CPU cost by program
panels.description: CPU time spent inside the BPF programs, summed over the selected cluster (1 = one full core). Empty unless sysctl kernel.bpf_stats_enabled=1 (adds ~20ns per program run).

targets.expr: sum by (config, program) (rate(ebpf_exporter_ebpf_program_run_time_seconds[$__rate_interval]) * on (id, instance) group_left (config, program) ebpf_exporter_ebpf_program_info)

panels.title: Exporter memory
panels.description: Exporter RSS per node, and kernel-function samples dropped because the 32k-address map is full (should stay 0).

targets.expr: max by (node) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job="ebpf-exporter"})
sum by (node) (rate(ebpf_exporter_node_kernel_function_samples_dropped_total[$__rate_interval]))
